q: For subdivision projects of one hectare or more, what portion of the gross area must be reserved as open space?
n: PD 1216 amended Sec. 31 of PD 957 to require 30% of the gross area as open space (roads, parks, playgrounds, schools and similar uses).
ref: PD 1216 (1977), Sec. 2, amending Sec. 31 of PD 957

q: What percentage of the gross area must be reserved for parks and playgrounds in high-density or social housing (66 to 100 family lots per gross hectare)?
n: The park and playground share follows housing density, not lot count in hectares: 9% for high density, 7% for medium density and 3.5% for low density.
ref: PD 1216 (1977), Sec. 2, amending Sec. 31 of PD 957

q: What percentage of the gross area must be reserved for parks and playgrounds in medium-density or economic housing (21 to 65 family lots per gross hectare)?
n: PD 1216 sets 7% for medium-density or economic housing.
ref: PD 1216 (1977), Sec. 2, amending Sec. 31 of PD 957

q: What percentage of the gross area must be reserved for parks and playgrounds in low-density or open-market housing (20 family lots and below per gross hectare)?
n: PD 1216 sets 3.5% for low-density or open-market housing.
ref: PD 1216 (1977), Sec. 2, amending Sec. 31 of PD 957

q: Under BP 220 (economic and socialized housing), what is the minimum frontage of a single-detached corner lot?
n: The BP 220 Table of Minimum Lot Frontage gives 8 m for corner and regular single-detached lots.
ref: BP 220, 2008 Revised IRR - Table on minimum lot frontage and lot area

q: Under BP 220, what is the minimum frontage of a single-detached interior lot?
n: BP 220 gives 3 m for an interior lot and 4 m for an irregular lot. PD 957 projects use larger frontages, so check which law governs the project.
ref: BP 220, 2008 Revised IRR - Table on minimum lot frontage and lot area

q: Under BP 220, what is the minimum frontage of an irregular single-detached lot?
n: Irregular lots are given 4 m in the BP 220 table.
ref: BP 220, 2008 Revised IRR - Table on minimum lot frontage and lot area

q: Under BP 220, what is the minimum lot frontage for a duplex or single-attached unit?
n: BP 220 sets 6 m for duplex and single-attached lots, for both economic and socialized housing.
ref: BP 220, 2008 Revised IRR - Table on minimum lot frontage and lot area

q: Under BP 220, what is the minimum frontage for a row-house lot in economic housing?
n: Economic housing needs 4 m and socialized housing 3.5 m for row houses. A row-house cluster is limited to 20 units and 100 m in length.
ref: BP 220, 2008 Revised IRR - Table on minimum lot frontage and lot area

q: Under PD 957 (open-market housing), what is the minimum frontage of a corner lot?
n: PD 957 sets 12 m for a corner lot in open-market housing; an inside lot is 10 m.
ref: PD 957 IRR (2009 Revised) - minimum lot requirements, open-market and medium-cost housing

q: Under BP 220, what is the minimum lot area for a single-detached unit in economic housing?
n: BP 220 sets 72 sqm for economic housing and 64 sqm for socialized housing.
ref: BP 220, 2008 Revised IRR - Table on minimum lot frontage and lot area

q: Under PD 957, what is the minimum lot area for a single-detached unit in open-market housing?
n: PD 957 gives 120 sqm for open-market housing and 100 sqm for medium-cost housing.
ref: PD 957 IRR (2009 Revised) - minimum lot requirements, open-market and medium-cost housing
